summary: T2-03 round 1: I ran all three story checks and each exited cleanly. pytest passed 140 tests, mypy found no issues, and make check (ruff, format, mypy) passed. The implementation uses an explicit unitary CIRCULAR_BASIS transform with no expanded formulas in the source. Both oracles are separate files. The required hypothesis test runs 200 examples of rank 1 to 3 covariances, and I saw no weakened or no-op tests. Only the story's files changed, and uv.lock and pyproject.toml are untouched. I did not read every test body, and I did not independently check the F6 and F7 numbers beyond the passing tests. One thing is only partly met: the open tolerance and threshold decisions are recorded in docstrings, not in a separate notes file.

checks.criterion: Check: uv run mypy pipeline/src pipeline/tests
checks.evidence: Success: no issues found in 10 source files
ruff check passed, 11 files already formatted, mypy found no issues in 11 source files

checks.criterion: Oracles are separate from polarimetry.py, with the stated tolerances (rtol=1e-10, atol=1e-12)
checks.evidence: pipeline/tests/polarimetry/expanded_oracle.py and jones_oracle.py both state they do not import terraluna_pipeline.polarimetry. ARITHMETIC_TOLERANCE is rtol 1e-10, atol 1e-12 (polarimetry.py:651). The failing-first run is not verifiable from the final tree, but the commit log shows test commits (bf6c876, bfe80b2) before the fix commit 4901f95.

checks.criterion: Fixtures assert Hermitian PSD first; F7 eigenvalues are checked
checks.evidence: Tests test_F6_fixture_is_a_rank_one_hermitian_psd_covariance (line 176) and test_F7_fixtures_are_hermitian_psd_with_the_prd_eigenvalues (line 186) exist and pass. The hypothesis test calls assert_hermitian_psd before using each covariance (line 929).

checks.criterion: F6 values (OC=0.25, SC_LL=0.49, SC_opp=0.09) and F7 values (CPR 3/19 versus 1, equal HH and HV powers, CPRs differ)
checks.evidence: Tests test_F6_matches_both_oracles, test_F7_matches_both_oracles, test_F7_same_hh_and_hv_powers_give_different_cpr and test_F7_two_channel_data_cannot_determine_cpr (lines 214 to 269) pass. I did not independently check the F6 and F7 numbers beyond these passing tests.

checks.criterion: Explicit unitary basis transform with the ordering and transmit vector stated in the docstring; no expanded formulas in the implementation; oracle comparison on F6, F7 and 200 random PSD covariances including SC_opp
checks.evidence: polarimetry.py:957-980 defines the unitary CIRCULAR_BASIS and the call at line 1302 is CIRCULAR_BASIS @ hermitian @ CIRCULAR_BASIS.conj().T. The docstring at lines 1172-1197 states both orderings and the transmit vector (1,-i)/sqrt2. The hypothesis test (test_polarimetry_covariance.py:923-971) uses max_examples=200, 1 to 3 scatterers, both conventions and both orderings.

checks.criterion: Required convention argument; unknown or missing raises; handedness_verified defaults to False; no Mini-RF-equivalent label
checks.evidence: circular_from_covariance (polarimetry.py:1260-1261) calls _check_ordering and _check_handedness_convention, which raise ValueError. handedness_verified defaults to False (line 1040). Tests at lines 338 to 403 cover both behaviours and pass.

checks.criterion: Invalid covariance cases give INVALID with distinct cause codes and no repair or clipping; PSD tolerance is an argument defaulting to the arithmetic tolerance; the open real-data PSD tolerance is recorded
checks.evidence: Rules at polarimetry.py:1268-1299 mark COV_NONFINITE, COV_NOT_HERMITIAN, COV_NEGATIVE_DIAGONAL and COV_NOT_PSD with no clipping. The tolerance argument defaults to ARITHMETIC_TOLERANCE (line 1168), and the docstring (lines 1201-1203) says the real-data tolerance is an open decision. Tests at lines 473 to 660 pass. The open decision is recorded only in docstrings, not in a separate notes file.

checks.criterion: OC<=0 gives CPR unavailable (OC_NONPOSITIVE, no epsilon); the handedness term and ratio are returned; base_SC<=0 makes the ratio unavailable; no 'not small' threshold in code, and the open decision is recorded
checks.evidence: polarimetry.py:1319 (OC_NONPOSITIVE), 1326-1328 (BASE_SC_NONPOSITIVE), and the docstring at lines 1195-1197 says no threshold is applied. Tests test_zero_oc_leaves_cpr_unavailable_without_an_epsilon, test_near_zero_oc_gets_no_epsilon and test_no_handedness_threshold_is_applied pass. The open decision is recorded in the docstring only.

checks.criterion: Scope and repo rules: changed files within the story's files list, nothing added to config/run.yaml, no uv.lock or pyproject.toml change
checks.evidence: The diff touches only polarimetry.py, pipeline/tests/polarimetry/{__init__,expanded_oracle,jones_oracle}.py and test_polarimetry_covariance.py. git status shows only a log file modified in the working tree.

findings.claim: The acceptance criteria say 'the notes record' the open real-data PSD tolerance and the open handedness threshold. These are recorded only in docstrings, and no notes file was changed.
findings.evidence: The diff contains no notes or docs file. The open decisions appear in the circular_from_covariance docstring (lines 1195-1203) and in ARITHMETIC_TOLERANCE (lines 651-654). The orchestrator may need to confirm this counts.

findings.claim: The criterion lists three cause codes (COV_NOT_HERMITIAN, COV_NOT_PSD, COV_NONFINITE). The implementation adds a fourth, COV_NEGATIVE_DIAGONAL, for a negative diagonal. It is distinct and INVALID, so this is probably acceptable.
findings.evidence: polarimetry.py:1289-1293 marks COV_NEGATIVE_DIAGONAL before the eigenvalue check. Tests test_negative_diagonal_beyond_the_tolerance_is_its_own_cause and test_each_invalid_case_has_a_distinct_cause pass.
